description: An oscillator that turns a picture into a wavetable: each row of the image becomes one waveform, and a scan control sweeps down the rows

params.text: Sets the pitch, from 10Hz at the far left to 10000Hz at the far right, and starts at 261.63Hz; in LFO mode the same travel covers 0.01Hz to 100Hz
Detunes the oscillator by up to a hundred cents either side of the pitch set by FREQ
Chooses which row of the picture is read as the waveform, the top row at the far left and the bottom row at the far right
Sets how much of the voltage at the SCAN jack is added to the SCAN knob, and reverses its sign anticlockwise of centre; at centre the jack does nothing
Sets how much of the voltage at the LIN FM jack reaches the frequency, none at the far left
Drops the pitch range to 0.01Hz through 100Hz, so the module works as a modulation source rather than an oscillator
Snaps FREQ to whole octaves above and below middle C instead of letting it run smoothly, and starts off
Picks what the SYNC jack does: in the up position an edge restarts the waveform from the beginning, in the down position it reverses the direction of travel instead

Opens the settings that turn the picture into waveforms: two smoothing sliders, how the rows are levelled, which way up they are read, whether flat rows are trimmed, and whether the result is inverted
Steps through which part of the picture's colour becomes the waveform: all three together, then red, then green, then blue; the four lamps beside it say which is chosen
Opens a short menu choosing where the picture comes from: an image file you pick, or the Nautiloid placed to the left of this module

inputs.text: Sets the pitch at a volt per octave, added to FREQ and FINE; the number of channels on this jack sets how many voices the module runs
Modulates the frequency as a fraction of the current pitch, scaled by the LIN FM knob; the signal is stripped of any steady offset first, so only its swing counts
Moves the scan down and up the picture, ten volts covering the whole image at the attenuverter's full setting; it is added to the SCAN knob and the total is held between the top and bottom rows
A rising edge above 1V restarts the waveform, or reverses it when SOFT is chosen

outputs.text: The row of the picture chosen by SCAN, read as a waveform at the pitch the module is set to, swinging ±5V
The same waveform a quarter of a cycle ahead of OUT, swinging ±5V

notes: with no picture loaded the module makes sound anyway: the built-in table sweeps sine to triangle to saw to square as SCAN is turned, which is also what Clear image puts back
the upper dark rectangle shows the picture the wavetable was made from, and the lower one draws the waveform currently being read; neither can be clicked
to use a fractal instead of a file, place a Nautiloid immediately to the left and choose it from the source button; panning and zooming the fractal then reshapes the table as you go
menu: Load image... — opens a file chooser for the picture the wavetable is built from
Reload image — reads the picture off disk again, picking up any change made to the file
Clear image — throws the picture away and goes back to the built-in sine, triangle, saw and square table
Embed image source in patch — saves the picture inside the patch file, so the patch sounds right on a machine that does not have the image
Seam smoothing — a slider setting how much the join between the end and start of each waveform is rounded off
Wave smoothing — a slider setting how much each waveform is smoothed along its length, trading detail for a quieter tone; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Normalize: Balanced, Global, Per row, Off — sets how the levels of the rows are evened out; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Row order: Top to bottom, Bottom to top — sets which end of the picture SCAN starts at; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Trim flat rows: Off, Gentle, Medium, Aggressive — drops rows of the picture with too little variation to make a waveform; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Per-row DC removal — takes the steady offset out of each row, so no waveform is off centre; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu
Invert conversion — turns the picture's light and dark the other way round before the waveforms are made; it is on the image options button, not the panel menu

inputs.2:
±10V · continuous · polyphonic

the knob and this input are summed and the total held to 0 to 10V.
inputs.3:
high above 1V · stepped · polyphonic
